places.label_why: "I have taken off my robe— must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?" The lines alternate A B A' B': two things she has done, each followed by a question about undoing it. The second line does not say the first again.

places.why: "My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him" tells an act and her response. The second line does not restate the first, and a bare narrative sequence is not a plain enough figure to go live as built on.

The five lines are a run of events, not lines opposed to each other, and "My heart sank at his departure" fits no contrast. Lines 4-5, "I sought him, but did not find him. / I called, but he did not answer", plainly say the same thing twice (sought/called, not find/not answer). Kept as said twice on those two lines.
places.label: form
places.label_why: "I sought him, but did not find him. / I called, but he did not answer." Calling is a second act and "he did not answer" a second failure, so the line adds to the first rather than restating it.

places.why: "I encountered the watchmen... They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak" is a narrative in which each line adds a new event. Nothing is restated, and no other form is plain here.

places.span_why: "How is your beloved better than others" is repeated in "How is your beloved better than another". "O most beautiful among women" only addresses her, and "that you charge us so" gives the reason for asking, so neither is a restatement.
places.label: all

places.why: "His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven" moves to a new feature with a new picture. It is one entry in a list of features, not a restatement, and as parallel lines nothing plain is shown.

"His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely" widens from one feature to the whole man, and "This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem" is a closing address. None of the four lines restates another.

places.span_why: "The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises" plainly say the same thing twice. The first two lines are a separate thought about her being unique.
places.label: form
places.label_why: "The maidens see her and call her blessed; / the queens and concubines sing her praises." The second line adds a different group from 6:8, the queens and concubines, who also praise her, so it builds on the first.

places.why: Lines 3-4, "Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim?", do not restate lines 1-2, so said twice does not fit the four lines. The plain figure is the doubled call "Come back, come back", the same word twice for force. Kept as doubling on those words.

"Your neck is like a tower... your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon... your nose is like the tower of Lebanon" give three likenesses for three different features. The lines are built alike but none restates another. The likenesses are a different figure at different words.

places.span_why: "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit" is a pair in which the second line completes the first. The wish that follows, "May your breasts be like clusters of the vine," is a separate pair of likenesses that runs on into the next verse.

places.why: "His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me": the second line adds the other arm to finish one picture. It does not restate the first, and a completed picture is not plain enough to go live as built on.

A question ("Who is this coming up from the wilderness...?") is followed by another speaker's words ("I roused you under the apple tree"). "There your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth" moves from conceiving to birth rather than restating. No said-twice is plain.

Lines 3-4 plainly set rebellion against the father's care: "I have raised children and brought them up, / but they have rebelled against Me." Lines 1-2 ("Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, / for the LORD has spoken") take no part in that contrast. The only tag, H0238 "give ear" in line 1, does not point at the figure.

"Your head has a massive wound, / and your whole heart is afflicted" plainly says the same thing twice (head/heart, wound/afflicted). The two questions ask about different things (beatings and rebelling) and do not restate the pair, so the span is lines 3-4.
places.label: all

places.span_why: "Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers" says the same thing twice, with foreigners and strangers. "Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire" names land, then cities, then fields, which adds items one by one rather than restating.
places.label: all

places.why: The second pair plainly restates the first: "Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; / listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!" This shows in the BSB, so the note that it shows only in the original is wrong. The single tag H0238 marks only "give ear" and none of the other paired words, so it is dropped.
places.label: form
places.label_why: "Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!" The four lines run A B A' B': hear and listen, then rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah.

places.why: "I am full from the burnt offerings of rams / and the fat of well-fed cattle; / I take no delight in the blood of bulls / and lambs and goats" plainly says the same thing twice. The opening question and the speech line "says the LORD" are not part of the pair, so the span is lines 3-6.
places.label: form
places.label_why: "I am full from the burnt offerings of rams / and the fat of well-fed cattle; / I take no delight in the blood of bulls / and lambs and goats." Lines 4 and 6 continue the lists in lines 3 and 5, so the lines alternate A B A' B' rather than each line saying the one before again.

places.why: "Though your sins are like scarlet" is not restated by "they will be as white as snow", which turns to the opposite. The four lines run A B A' B' (scarlet/crimson, snow/wool), so Alternating lines fits better than "Said twice".

"She once was full of justice; / righteousness resided within her, / but now only murderers!" plainly sets the present against the past. Line 1, "See how the faithful city has become a harlot!", is a heading whose contrast sits inside one line, so the span is lines 2-4.
places.span_why: "She once was full of justice" set against "but now only murderers!" is the plain opposite of once and now. "righteousness resided within her" restates the first line and does not oppose it, so it is left out.

places.why: "I will thoroughly purge your dross; / I will remove all your impurities" plainly say the same thing twice (purge/remove, dross/impurities). "I will turn My hand against you" introduces the act rather than restating it, so the span is lines 2-3.
places.label: all

places.why: The plain pair is "For the law will go forth from Zion, / and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem" (law/word of the LORD, Zion/Jerusalem). Marking all seven lines, from "And many peoples will come and say:" on, is too wide. The figure is plain in the BSB, so "only in the original" is wrong. The tag H3068G also lights "the LORD" in line 2, outside the figure, so the tags are dropped.
places.label: all

places.span_why: The verse has three separate pairs: judging the nations, beating weapons into tools, and an end to war. They do not restate one another. The clearest pair is "They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks."
places.label: form
places.label_why: "They will beat their swords into plowshares / and their spears into pruning hooks." The second line has no verb of its own. It completes the first by adding a second weapon and tool, so it builds on the first rather than saying it again.

places.why: "For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob" is the verdict, and the lines after it give its reasons. Each reason adds a new charge ("influences from the east", "soothsayers like the Philistines", "strike hands with the children of foreigners"), so nothing is plainly restated.

places.span_why: "Their land is full of silver and gold, with no limit to their treasures" restates itself within the pair. The pair about horses and chariots is about a different thing, military strength, so it does not say the first pair again.
places.label: all

places.why: "The proud look of man will be humbled, / and the loftiness of men brought low" plainly says the same thing twice. Line 3, "the LORD alone will be exalted in that day", sets the opposite against them, so it is left out of the span.
places.label: all

places.span_why: "the young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable" plainly says the same thing twice. The opening lines about people oppressing one another are a different thought, not a restatement of it.

places.why: "their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; their perfume bottles and charms" is one stretch of a list of finery that runs from 3:18 to 3:23. The second line names new items and does not restate the first.

Each exchange is a different one ("instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness"), so the lines do not restate one another. "Instead of fragrance / there will be a stench" is also one clause split over two lines. The plain figure is the fivefold opening "instead of". Kept as like beginnings, marking each clause's opening.

"Whoever remains in Zion / and whoever is left in Jerusalem" plainly restates in the BSB, not only in the original. "Will be called holy" and the last line are the predicate and stand outside the pair. The tags fall on holy, said, every, recorded and life, which do not carry the pair, and leave "remains" (H7604) untagged.

places.why: "when the Lord has washed away / the filth of the daughters of Zion / and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem" plainly restates in the BSB. The last line, "by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire", gives the means and is not part of the pair. Two of the tags are the object marker H0853, while "washed" and "cleanse" are untagged, so the tags are dropped.

places.why: "He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, / but the fruit it produced was sour!" plainly sets good against sour. Lines 1-4 ("He dug it up... dug out a winepress as well") list the owner's work with no contrast, so the span is lines 5-6.

"I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled" says the same judgment twice, with hedge matching wall and consumed matching trampled. The opening line "Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard:" only introduces the pair, so it is no longer marked.

places.label_why: The lines alternate: "I will take away its hedge, / and it will be consumed; / I will tear down its wall, / and it will be trampled". Hedge and wall match, consumed and trampled match, but line 3 does not say line 2 again.

places.why: No line restates another. The plain figure is the likeness "As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land", so it is kept as a simile with only those words marked.

"state a proposal, but it will not happen" says "Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted" again (plan/proposal, thwarted/not happen). The "but" sits inside each line, so this is not opposite. "For God is with us" is the reason and is left out.

places.why: "Many will stumble over these; they will fall and be broken; they will be ensnared and captured" goes a step further in each line (stumble, then fall and break, then be trapped). The lines build; none simply restates the one before.

"The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel" is one event said twice, with Jacob/Israel paired. This is plain in the BSB itself, so the claim that it shows only in the original is wrong. The tags are also lopsided: they mark "fall" but not "word" or "sent". The tags are stripped and the BSB lines stand on their own.

places.label_why: "The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, / and it has fallen upon Israel": the second line continues from the first ("it" is the message) and tells what happened next, that it landed. It does not just say the first again.

places.why: "they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied" restates "They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry" (right/left, hungry/not satisfied). Nothing is set as an opposite. Line 5 adds a new thing and is left out.

places.label_why: The lines alternate: "They carve out what is on the right, / but they are still hungry; / they eat what is on the left, / but they are still not satisfied". Right and left match, hungry and not satisfied match.

"they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; they will not look with pity on the children" is a plain restatement (no mercy/no pity, fruit of the womb/children). "Their bows will dash young men to pieces" names other victims and a deed, so it is left out.
